drafts.walkScript: Start with brave. Brave means not giving in to fear. Fearless means without fear, so it matches. Reckless goes too far, cowardly is the opposite, and loyal means something else.
Start with swift. Swift means moving fast. Speedy means fast too, so it matches. Instant means no time at all, which goes too far. Sudden and early are about when, not speed.
Start with damp. Damp means a little wet. Moist also means a little wet, so it matches. Soaked is far too wet. Mouldy and cold can go with damp but mean something else.
Start with chilly. Chilly means a little cold. Cool also means a little cold, so it matches. Freezing is far too cold. Shivery and grey can go with chilly days but mean something else.

Start with shiny. Shiny means catching the light and looking bright. Gleaming means the same, so it matches. Dazzling is so bright it hurts to look at, which is too strong. Smooth and new things are often shiny, but the words mean something else.

Start with glad. Glad means happy about something. Pleased means just the same, so it matches. Overjoyed is much too strong. Relieved means a worry has ended, and lucky means things went well by chance.
Start with hollow. Hollow means having nothing inside. Empty also means nothing inside, so it matches. Solid is the opposite. Light and wooden can describe hollow things but mean something else.
Start with huge. Huge means very, very big. Enormous means the same, so it matches. Big is not strong enough. Tall and heavy each name only one way to be big.
Start with rapid. Rapid means very fast. Quick means fast too, so it matches. Slow is the opposite, and a race is a thing, not a speed. Hurried means rushing because time is short.

Start with generous. Generous means happy to give to others. Giving means the same, so it matches. Extravagant means spending far too much. Friendly and wealthy people may be generous, but the words mean something else.
Start with gloomy. Gloomy means low and unhappy. Miserable means the same, so it matches. Despairing goes much further, with all hope gone. Grumpy means cross, and silent only means making no sound.
Start with timid. Timid means easily scared and shy. Shy means the same, so it matches. Terrified is far too strong. Quiet is only one part of timid, and polite means something else.

Start with rare. Rare means not found often. Uncommon means just that, so it matches. Unique means the only one, which goes too far. Strange and precious things may be rare, but the words mean something else.
Start with sturdy. Sturdy means strong and well made. Strong is the closest, so it matches. Unbreakable goes too far. Heavy and wooden things can be sturdy, but the words mean something else.

Start with bold. Bold means brave enough to take a risk. Daring means the same, so it matches. Reckless goes too far, with no care for danger. Stubborn means refusing to change, and famous means well known.

Start with ancient. Ancient means very old. Old is the closest, so it matches. Prehistoric goes too far back, to before anything was written down. Ruined and valuable can describe ancient things but mean something else.
Start with hostile. Hostile means acting like an enemy. Unfriendly is the closest, so it matches. Murderous is far too strong. Rude means bad manners, and frowning is only one sign of it.
Start with humble. Humble means not thinking too much of yourself. Modest means the same, so it matches. Proud is the opposite. Quiet is only one part of it, and grateful means thankful.
Start with vague. Vague means not clear or exact. Unclear means the same, so it matches. Meaningless goes too far. Mysterious means hard to explain, and brief only means short.
Start with feeble. Feeble means weak, with little strength. Frail means the same, so it matches. Helpless goes too far. Pale and elderly can go with feeble, but the words mean something else.
Start with genuine. Genuine means truly what it claims to be. Real means the same, so it matches. Fake is the opposite. Signed and costly things may be genuine, but the words mean something else.

Start with reluctant. Reluctant means not wanting to do something. Unwilling means the same, so it matches. Opposed goes further, as it means firmly against. Doubtful means unsure, and slow only describes speed.
Start with obedient. Obedient means doing what you are told. Well-behaved is the closest, so it matches. Naughty is the opposite. Polite means good manners, and quiet is only one part of it.

Start with trivial. Trivial means not mattering much. Unimportant means the same, so it matches. Worthless goes too far, as it means of no value at all. Small things can be trivial, but small is about size.

Start with JUBILANT in the sentence. JUBILANT means very happy and full of joy. Overjoyed means the same, so it matches. Pleased is not strong enough. Noisy is only one part, and relieved means a worry has ended.

Start with RECEDE in the sentence. Floodwater that recedes moves back from where it spread. Retreat also means moving back, so it matches. Vanish goes too far, and settle means grow still. Fade is another meaning, used for sounds or memories.

Start with CONCEAL in the sentence. She tried to stop her friends seeing her disappointment. Hide means the same, so it matches. Show is the opposite. Ignore means not paying attention, and pretend means acting as if something is true.

Start with EXHAUSTED in the sentence. After a long walk, it means very tired, with no energy left. Drained means the same, so it matches. Lively is the opposite, and sleepy means wanting to sleep. Empty fits another meaning, as when all the food is used up.

Start with AMEND in the sentence. To amend writing means to make changes to it. Change is the closest, so it matches. Rewrite goes too far, as it means writing it all again. Shorten is only one kind of change, and check means look over.

Start with FUTILE in the sentence. FUTILE means having no use or result. Pointless means the same, so it matches. Successful is the opposite. Impossible goes too far, and foolish means silly, not useless.

Start with AMIABLE in the sentence. It means friendly and pleasant to be with. Friendly is the closest, so it matches. Grumpy is the opposite. Cheerful means happy, and chatty is only one part of being friendly.
Start with ABUNDANT in the sentence. It means there were lots of fish. Plentiful means the same, so it matches. Rare is the opposite, and endless goes too far. Large is about size, not how many.

Start with NOTORIOUS in the sentence. It means well known for something bad. Infamous means the same, so it matches. Famous misses the bad part, and unknown is the opposite. Dangerous fits the road, but does not mean well known.

Start with EXQUISITE in the sentence. It means very beautiful and finely made. Beautiful is the closest, so it matches. Pretty is not strong enough, and costly means something else. Sharp fits another meaning, as in a sharp pain.

Start with BENEVOLENT in the sentence. It means kind and wanting to do good. Kind means the same, so it matches. Saintly goes too far. Polite means good manners, and wealthy is about money, not kindness.

Start with STOIC in the sentence. It means staying calm and not showing upset. Calm is the closest, so it matches. Tearful is the opposite. Stubborn means refusing to change, and silent is only one part of it.
Start with JOVIAL in the sentence. It means cheerful and friendly. Cheerful means the same, so it matches. Ecstatic is far too strong. Silly means foolish, and loud is only one part of it.

Start with TRANSPARENT in the sentence. It means see-through, as the cake could be seen inside. Clear means the same, so it matches. Thin is only one part of it, and shiny is not see-through. Obvious is used for ideas, not for a lid.

Start with LUMINOUS in the sentence. It means giving off light, so the dial shows in the dark. Glowing means the same, so it matches. Blazing is far too strong. Pale means faint in colour, and visible only means it can be seen.
Start with MELANCHOLY in the sentence. It means sad and thoughtful. Sad is the closest, so it matches. Heartbroken is far too strong. A gentle or slow tune is not always sad.
Start with brave. Brave means not giving in to fear. Courageous means the same, so it matches. Cautious means careful, curious means wanting to know, and clumsy means awkward.
